verdict.rationale: LangGraph's checkpointer/persistence system supports 'time travel' — replaying and resuming from prior state — and interrupts allow human review/modification of in-flight execution, which the community explicitly confirms as a way to fix and roll back an analyst's step (langgraph-comm-2, langgraph-docs-2, langgraph-docs-25). However, this addresses run-time state rollback, not versioning of the automation/graph definition itself (e.g., deployed graph revisions, diffing/rolling back workflow code changes), which is not evidenced anywhere in the pack. Missing for 10: explicit graph/automation versioning, a version history or diff UI for workflows, and rollback to a prior deployed graph version (as opposed to just state checkpoints).
